To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the mass variables M_{T2} and M_{W} are useful in the VBF Higgs search at the LHC and that the mass variables are complementary in the sense that they are useful at different Higgs mass values.

(i) the mass variable mT2 is a promising candidate for the separation of the Higgs signal from background processes; (ii) the mass variable M2T is a promising candidate to separate the Higgs signal and the WZ background; (iii) the mass variable MT2 is not useful to separate the Higg signal from the background; (iv) the mass variables mT2 and M2T are not useful to separate Higgs and WZ signal from the background.

the mass variables M_{T2} and M_{CT}, as well as their combination M_{CT}+M_{T2}, are useful for the vector boson-fusion production of a Higgs boson at the LHC, and that M_{CT} is the most powerful variable for the separation of signal and background in the case of a Higgs resonance with spin zero.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the vector boson production of the Higgs at the CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in the final state with two jets, two leptons and missing energy, where the leptons are either electrons or muons.
the production of a Higgs boson at the LHC in association with two jets and missing transverse energy, and with the subsequent decay of the Higgs into a lepton pair.

the following topics: (1) the development of a Monte Carlo event generator for the vector boson scattering production of a Higgs boson, (2) the investigation of the mass variables in the context of the vector boson process, (3) the study of the mass variables for the Higgs signal in the presence of the dominant backgrounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a spin zero WW signal is not required for a significant discovery.
the mass variables are not very useful in the case of vector boson fusion Higgs production.
there exists a region where the Higgs can be observed in the two jet channel, but only at the price of assuming a spin zero resonance in order to reduce the background to a manageable level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the signal can be extracted with a high degree of confidence in the presence of backgrounds.
the mass variables do indeed improve the signal to noise ratio.
we have shown that the use of mass variables in conjunction with the two jet plus di-lepton final state can lead to an improvement in sensitivity for the Higgs search.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Higgs signal is very different from the WW continuum, which is a very good thing.
the mass variable $m_{T2}$, which was developed to search for supersymmetric particles, may be a useful variable to use in this search for the Higgs boson.
there is a region in phase space where the Higgs mass and the invariant mass of the two jets can be reconstructed with a resolution which is comparable to the width of the Higgs.
